KEY_FINDINGS.FINDING-1: MoR recursion is the dominant source of computational overhead AND gradient explosions at seq_len=64. Removing MoR gives 2× throughput, 50% VRAM reduction, 80% fewer explosions with no statistically significant loss change.
KEY_FINDINGS.FINDING-2: LR warmup schedule (0–200 steps) has ZERO effect on gradient explosion frequency. Root cause is architectural (MoR), not optimizer warm-up. No warmup strategy will fix this.
KEY_FINDINGS.FINDING-3: Titans memory adds 20% VRAM overhead with no short-sequence benefit. Benefit hypothesis requires seq_len>=512 validation.
KEY_FINDINGS.FINDING-4: Dense Transformer baseline converges 2.3× lower loss in 50 steps BUT runs 75× faster. Compute-controlled comparison is required before drawing architectural conclusions.
KEY_FINDINGS.FINDING-5: Backward pass dominates IVERI training time (70% of wall-clock). Gradient checkpointing adds 31% overhead at seq_len=64, safely disabled at this scale.
